identification: Cased 12-coin 'History of Seafaring' proof set (Beschichte der Schifffahrt/Histoire de la navigation), wooden presentation case, capsuled crown-size coins with tall ships, from Pacific/African issuers (Cook Islands/Tuvalu $2, Vanuatu 10 vatu, PNG 2 kina, 1 dollar Royal Clipper, 100 francs). Looks like the 2008-2010 multi-country series; the Noble 2012 'History of Seafaring silver crowns' suggests at least some issues are silver, but a 12-piece set may mix silver and silver-plated base metal. Fineness not readable in photos.

Also search 'History of Seafaring' Noble Numismatics, Leski, Downies, Mowbray, Heritage past results, and LiveAuctioneers/Invaluable 'History of Seafaring proof set'. Check issuer (Numista 'History of Seafaring' series, 2008-2010 Cook Islands/Tuvalu/Vanuatu/PNG/Belarus) for composition: .925 silver vs silver-plated copper-nickel, and the original issue price from the mint/dealer.
viewing_check: Read the edge and reverse of several coins out of capsule if allowed: fineness marks (925, Ag, 'silver', weight 28.28g/1oz or 31.1g), look for certificate of authenticity in the case lid or under the tray, and check a magnet test and weight on a couple of coins. Plated cupronickel is near worthless; .925 crown coins are roughly melt plus modest premium. Photograph any certificate and the case underside.
